card.name: Verbs and links after a subject clause
card.fires_on: Words right after a subject or clause where a past-tense verb, link word or reporting verb comes next, such as 'found', 'saw', 'was', 'when', 'and'. Mostly in news-style or study-results prose describing what was observed.

modes.label: Reporting verb after researchers
modes.description: A verb of finding or observing follows a research subject.
modes.example: The researchers<< saw>> no sign of such a wobble.

modes.label: Link word in a running sentence
modes.description: A joining word like 'and', 'when', 'without' or 'to' continues a clause about an event or finding.
modes.example: He repeated those concerns<< when>> he learned of WCS's findings in northern

modes.label: Study results wording
modes.description: A word inside a results or safety statement about patients or animals.
modes.example: and there<< was>> no evidence of harm to the animal fetus

card.writes: It favors 'will' and Chinese future-tense words 'will be', and suppresses Chinese past-result verbs, so it pushes toward a verb of what happens or will happen next.
card.plain: It fires on the small word or verb after a subject, where the sentence is about to say what someone found or what happened.
